source.title: Effect of Delayed Diagnosis of Phenylketonuria With Imaging Findings of Bilateral Diffuse Symmetric White Matter Lesions: A Case Report and Literature Review.

confirmation.summary: Markedly raised blood phenylalanine (1221.5 μM) and PAH variants c.1068C>A and c.740G>T.
evidence: significantly elevated Phe levels (1221.5μM, Phe/Tyr ratio 27.45) in blood
Heterozygous mutations exist in gene encoding PAH c.1068C>A and c.740G>T

note.text: My older brother had a fit when he was three and has struggled to think and count ever since; he never went to school. Over the last two months he has had trouble judging where things are and finding his way, and his personality has changed. He can no longer walk steadily. He sweats a lot, has trouble passing urine and is constipated. His legs are stiff and weak, and his hands shake.
note.author: Peter's Kiro, written from the article's findings; not the family's words

uncertainty: The note says 'his hands shake'; the article reports tremor without naming the body site.
The article reports a family history of intellectual disability; the note is written as if by a sibling, which is a framing choice, not a source fact.
